Ridge Modification of the Hessian

Source: R/modify.R
modify_ridge.Rd

Builds the modification that adds a multiple of the identity, \(\tilde H = H + \tau I\). The shift starts at \(\tau = \max(\texttt{floor},\; \texttt{floor} - \min_i H_{ii})\), which makes the diagonal positive, and is doubled until the Cholesky factorization of \(\tilde H\) succeeds (at most 60 times; the identity matrix is used if none succeeds). This is the idea of Levenberg: the direction moves from the Newton direction at \(\tau = 0\) to a scaled steepest-descent direction for large \(\tau\). It costs less than modify_eigen() and shifts every eigenvalue, not only the small ones.

Usage

modify_ridge(floor = 1e-08)

Arguments

floor

The smallest shift, a single positive number. Defaults to 1e-8.

Value

An S7 object of class ModifyRidge, inheriting from hessian_modification(), with the properties floor and label.

See also

modify_eigen(), modifications for the comparison, hessian_modify(), newton(), chebyshev()

Examples

m <- modify_ridge(floor = 1e-6)
m
#> <hessian_modification> ridge (floor = 1e-06)

# The method for hessian_modify() applied to an indefinite matrix.
H <- matrix(c(2, 1, 1, -3), 2, 2)
eigen(hessian_modify(m, H), only.values = TRUE)$values
#> [1] 8.192584 2.807420

# Passed to the optimizer.
f <- function(p) p[1]^4 - 2 * p[1]^2 + p[2]^2
g <- function(p) c(4 * p[1]^3 - 4 * p[1], 2 * p[2])
h <- function(p) matrix(c(12 * p[1]^2 - 4, 0, 0, 2), 2, 2)
minimize(newton(modify = modify_ridge(floor = 1e-6)), f, c(0.05, 0.6),
         gr = g, hess = h)
#> <optimizer_result> Newton
#>   value      : -1
#>   par        : 1 0
#>   iterations : 4   evaluations: f 5, g 5
#>   elapsed    : 0 us
#>   converged  : yes (gradient (max-norm) < 1e-06 or |df| < 1e-10 or |dx| < 1e-08)
